page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 12 vCPUs and 128 GB of RAM. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.0 GHz with 12 physical cores and a shared CPU allocation. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are handled by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is rated as average to strong, with Geekbench multi-core scores in the top 25%. Memory performance is robust, showing strong large-block read and write bandwidth in the top 25%. In LLM inference tests, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 368.6 tokens per second for small models and strong speeds of 35.15 tokens per second for medium models.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage solutions. However, the high density of GPU resources relative to the CPU count makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that rely heavily on GPU acceleration rather than sustained multi-core CPU execution. It is highly suited for LLM inference, machine learning workloads, data science tasks, and GPU-accelerated rendering.
description: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server featuring 12 vCPUs, 128 GB of RAM, and two NVIDIA L40S GPUs with 96 GB of total VRAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-based instance offers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong memory bandwidth. While the CPU allocation is shared and local storage is absent, the server delivers exceptional GPU capabilities, as evidenced by top-tier text generation speeds in small LLM inference benchmarks. This configuration is highly efficient for workloads that prioritize GPU acceleration over local disk storage, making it well-suited for machine learning, LLM inference, and data science applications.
